detailed_rationale:
Hexaware Technologies is the IT services company that Baring Private Equity Asia took private in 2021 and re-listed via IPO in early 2025 -- which is why the quant scorecard has almost no fundamental fields populated for it (zero_cov_flag is set) and is leaning heavily on price/technical signals rather than balance-sheet data. Independent research fills that gap with a picture that is genuinely good on quality: trailing ROE of ~23.5%, ROIC near 29%, net margin ~10%, and a net-cash balance sheet (~Rs 20.9 bn cash versus ~Rs 7.1 bn debt) -- these are strong, not marginal, metrics for a mid-tier IT services company. Hexaware reports on a calendar-year basis (not the April-March fiscal year most Indian IT peers use); Q2 CY2026 revenue was $405.4 million, up 6.1% YoY and 4.4% QoQ in constant currency, with EBIT margin at 13.6%, within the guided 13-14% band.

The reason this is not an easy rescue: management just cut full-year CY2026 revenue-growth guidance to 6-7% from a prior 7.6%, explicitly citing delayed deal ramps and macro pressure concentrated in the Travel & Transportation vertical. That is a fresh, company-specific negative data point on the exact metric (growth) that matters most for a stock trading near 24-25x trailing earnings -- a PEG-type read of roughly 3.5-4x on the newly trimmed growth rate is not obviously cheap. Sector-wide, the skill's own quick-note on IT flags constant-currency growth versus headline and GenAI pricing risk as the things to watch, and a guidance cut into that backdrop is exactly the kind of signal that should weigh against optimism, not be waved through on the strength of good historical ROE.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score is Sell on the 3-year lens (21.32) while the 1-year composite (49.73) already sits in Hold territory -- but that 1-year score is built on very incomplete data (coverage_1y of only ~57%, largely price/ownership signals rather than fundamentals, given zero_cov_flag). My own research finds genuinely strong quality metrics (ROE ~23%, net cash), which is the kind of finding that would normally support a rescue. I am not exercising it here because there is a fresh, specific, company-sourced negative catalyst -- the guidance cut to 6-7% growth, announced on the most recent earnings call -- that directly undercuts the growth assumption embedded in a ~24-25x multiple. A quality balance sheet does not offset a fresh growth-guidance cut at a full-ish multiple; I am keeping the Sell rather than treating good historical ROE as sufficient grounds to override.
summary: Hexaware Technologies is an IT services company that re-listed on the Indian markets in early 2025 after several years under private-equity ownership. The underlying business is financially strong -- healthy returns on capital, no net debt, and margins within its own guided range -- but management has just trimmed its full-year revenue growth guidance, citing delayed deal ramps and pressure in its travel-sector client base. That combination of a fresh guidance cut against a valuation that was not obviously cheap to begin with is the reason for caution here.
positive_para: Return on equity (~23.5% trailing) and return on invested capital (~29%) are genuinely strong for an IT services company, the balance sheet carries no net debt, and EBIT margin (13.6% in the latest quarter) is within management's own guided 13-14% band -- this is a well-run, well-capitalized business, not a weak one.
negative_para: Management just cut full-year CY2026 revenue growth guidance to 6-7% from a prior 7.6%, citing delayed deal ramps and macro pressure concentrated in the Travel & Transportation vertical -- a fresh, specific negative signal on the exact metric that matters for the stock's multiple. At a trailing PE in the mid-20s for a business now guiding mid-single-digit growth, the valuation is not clearly cheap enough to absorb further guidance disappointments, and the broader IT sector faces genuine GenAI-linked deal-pricing uncertainty that is not specific to Hexaware alone.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a trailing PE near 24-25x against freshly-guided growth of 6-7%, the implied PEG of roughly 3.5-4x is rich for the growth rate now on the table, even allowing for the quality premium a 23%+ ROE, net-cash balance sheet reasonably commands. The business can clear a modest growth bar comfortably given its capital efficiency, but the current multiple looks priced for something closer to the higher growth guidance management just walked back from, not the 6-7% now on offer -- this reads as fair-to-rich rather than cheap.
